Hi Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned with ACME's procurement and security gating items. I captured the parts that looked like hard blockers vs. nice-to-haves.

1) Primary blockers (need resolution before procurement):
   - SOC 2 attestation or SOC-equivalent summary for our hosted offering (scoped to data processed for ACME).
   - Audit log retention guarantees (retention windows + log export formats).
   - Data Processing Agreement (DPA) redlines from your legal team (we reviewed the high-level asks today).
   - Pen test evidence & remediation summary — your InfoSec wants confirmation of remediation cadence.

2) Goals you stated:
   - Complete security review and legal sign-off within four weeks so ACME can start a POC in prod-like environment in May.
   - Retention policies that meet your regulatory needs (7 years for certain artifacts), with exported log samples for ingestion into your SIEM.

3) What we committed to deliver by next touch:
   - Redwood: share SOC 2 summary + a sanitized pen-test executive summary (attachments). Owner: Aditya. Due: 2026-04-13 EOD.
   - Redwood: provide an export of representative audit-log rows and a short schema doc. Owner: Marissa. Due: 2026-04-14 noon PT.
   - Redwood: send a DPA with tracked changes addressing your two primary redlines (data residency + subprocessor notice). Owner: Legal via Vivek (cc'd). Due: 2026-04-15.

Action items for ACME: please confirm the list of required artifacts (SOC 2 vs. SOC-equivalent reporting), and share any mandatory clause text you need in the DPA. If possible, have your procurement/Legal send a single consolidated redline to speed turnaround.

I attached the SOC2 summary and pen-test exec summary to this message (redacted for customer distribution); full reports require an NDA which we can escalate if needed. I've also dropped the audit-log sample and a Drive folder with the evidence pack here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_security_pack

If this matches your notes, next step: Laura, can we target a short call Wednesday (30m) to review the DPA redlines and confirm timeline? I can bring our Legal and Infra leads.

Best,

Aditya —

Thanks for the detailed recap. That aligns well with our internal notes. A few clarifications/questions from my side:

- SOC 2: we can accept a SOC 2 Type II report or a SOC-equivalent third-party assessment. If you only have a summary available publicly, we'll need an NDA to review the full report.
- Audit logs: we need schema + monthly export options. The sample rows look good but can you confirm whether logs include user_id (pseudonymous) and request payload hashes (not full payloads)?
- Retention: our compliance group needs a written guarantee for retention durations and deletion procedures — 7 years for some financial artifacts is typical for us.
- DPA redlines: I'll get our Legal to produce one consolidated tracked-change doc by COB tomorrow.

Tom (CISO) — can you join the DPA + pen-test review on Wednesday if we set it up?

Appreciate the fast follow-up.

Thanks Laura — adding a few specifics on the audit logs and retention so ACME's compliance can evaluate: 

- Audit log contents: timestamp (UTC), request_id, user_id (pseudonymized internal id), model_id, input_hash, response_metadata (token counts, latency), and outcome status codes. We do not include full request payloads in exported logs unless explicitly requested with contract controls.
- Export format: CSV or JSONL, compressed, delivered via S3 presigned URL or Secure FTP (your preference).
- Retention windows: configurable per-customer. Default: 90 days hot, 365 days cold; longer-term archival (up to 7 years) is available as a paid retention policy — documented SLA and deletion playbook provided.

Attached is a small sample (audit_log_sample_rows.csv) and a one-page schema. If ACME requires different fields, we can map them in the POC export.

Action: Aditya — once Laura's Legal sends the DPA redline, Vivek and I will triage internal controls and get back with a proposed response timeline.

-Marissa

2) 48 hours: Redwood Legal review + high-level response to material clauses (Vivek).
3) 5 business days: technical confirmation on retention/export mechanics + sanitized SOC2/pen-test artifacts for ACME to review (Marissa).
4) Within 2 weeks: joint security call (ACME CISO + Redwood Infra) to close any remaining technical gaps and confirm POC sign-off criteria.

Deliverables we will attach to the Docusign packet / Drive folder:

- SOC2 summary + instructions for requesting full report under an NDA.
- Pen-test exec summary & remediation log.

If this cadence works, I'll assign a single Redwood point of contact for legal follow-up (that's me) and Marissa will be the security lead for the POC data exports. Aditya will coordinate scheduling and commercial items.

Next meeting suggestion: 2026-04-22 at 10:00 PT — 30 minutes. Laura / Tom, does that time work?

Thanks — Vivek
